requirements.description: An ante reveals two player cards and a three-card flop before a fold or call of twice the ante, followed by turn, river, dealer qualification at a pair of fours, and transparent best-five-card settlement.
requirements.notes: Issue #77 allocates the permanent distinct rules requirement for issue #139.

requirements.description: Authenticated sessions own private reload-safe decision rounds, hidden dealer cards and unrevealed community cards, durable receipts, settled history, and canonical route restoration.
requirements.notes: Session context overrides caller player ids, private cards remain hidden until settlement, and committed results survive reload and process restart.

requirements.description: Ante and call debits plus returned-token settlement credits use the shared ledger exactly once under durable action identities, while folds add no token movement.
requirements.notes: No game code mutates balances directly and conflicting retries fail closed.

requirements.description: Casino Hold'em supplies complete English and Russian responsive, accessible, reduced-motion-safe, timer-clean play.
requirements.notes: Evidence covers both locales and every governed viewport.

requirements.description: Catalog, contract, browser, and long-suite discovery include Casino Hold'em with requirement, module, version, and visual traceability.
requirements.notes: Descriptor sort order 290 and the catalog-discovered long driver are canonical.

requirements.description: The Casino Hold'em data rail displays the server-owned ante payout schedule (royal flush 100:1 through the even-money band at 1:1) in both en-US and ru-RU, sourced from the published ante_return_multipliers rules payload rather than duplicated client constants.
requirements.notes: Issue #253 (Casino Hold'em half): mirrors the merged Caribbean Stud disclosure; the schedule renders only when the server publishes it.

requirements.description: Casino Hold'em publishes deal preparation, action receipts, Call or Fold decisions, ledger proof, terminal archive, settlement recovery, and action-owned rollback through provider-current callbacks that replace only active round, recent rounds, and action receipts. Competing processes preserve unrelated player-state siblings and fail closed before stale decisions can overwrite or resurrect a terminal round, while lost ledger responses reconcile immutable proof without repeating a debit or credit.
requirements.notes: The frozen v1 routes, cards, ranking, paytables, dealer privacy, and ledger vocabulary remain unchanged. Production multiworker activation stays blocked because state, ledger, and history remain separate transaction boundaries.
